The prompt explicitly warns against the "fat" case being unreachable due to scale (run29 example). By starting with a **Linear/Rigorous Polynomial Family** (e.g., $f(x) = ax+b$) vs. a **High-Degree Fat Family** (e.g., $f(x) = \sum_{k=0}^{10} a_k x^k$), we establish the fundamental validity of the "Zero Violation" metric and the capacity scan infrastructure. Once the linear case proves $N_c$ is small and flat (rigid), we can confidently attribute failures in the fat case to intrinsic solution space dimensionality ($N_c = \infty$) rather than numerical instability or scaling issues, satisfying the "Step 0: Rigidity Accessibility Bootstrap" requirement. This aligns with the past knowledge logs (iter 80, 53, 13) which focus on implementing the rigid polynomial family.

steps.description: Implement the family(kind, w, seed) function to generate training and held-out constraint points for rigid (linear) and fat (high-degree polynomial) families. The function must return normalized y/yv arrays with shape (N,1), ensure X and Xv are disjoint, and apply O(1) normalization to satisfy the 1e-3 zero-violation criterion. This enables the capacity_scan infrastructure to verify N_c for the rigid family and confirm the fat family is unreachable (N_c = ∞).
